podcast.body: David Bowie began writing this song three days after Richard Nixon's resignation in August 1974, and it was released in 1975. The song is described not as an anti-Nixon track but rather as an observation on the state of post-Nixon America. It includes a direct question, "Do you remember your president Nixon? Do you remember you have bills to pay?", suggesting a contemplation on whether the public would remember the disgraced president or the circumstances of his departure. "He seems to be asking if anyone will eventually care that Nixon resigned in disgrace In other words will we ever remember how we got here?"

The title track and lead single from Bowie's 1975 album, "Young Americans" was a seminal stylistic pivot, where Bowie fully embraced "Plastic Soul" and American R&B. It featured collaborators like Carlos Alomar and Luther Vandross, peaked at number 28 on the Hot 100 in the spring of 1975, and included a lyrical reference to The Beatles' "A Day in the Life" sung by the Vandross-led chorus. "Young Americans remains one of the great stylistic pivots by any artist in rock history. Boey fully committed to what he called Plastic Soul, going deep on his love of American R&B for the first time since the mid-60s."
